ground_truth_methodology: Established by directly reading the cloned source at the pinned commit (Read/Grep on benchmarks/real_world_python/repos/fastapi), verified line-for-line against the actual clone. Veyra was NOT used to produce any of this file.

queries.query: Where is the FastAPI application class defined, and what does it extend?
queries.expected_answer_summary: fastapi.applications.FastAPI, defined at applications.py:42, subclasses Starlette (from the separate starlette package, an external dependency).

queries.query: Which class represents a single registered API route (path + handler + metadata)?
queries.expected_answer_summary: fastapi.routing.APIRoute, defined at routing.py:1126, subclassing starlette.routing.Route.

queries.query: Where is the Depends() function used for dependency injection defined?
queries.expected_answer_summary: fastapi.param_functions.Depends, defined at param_functions.py:2283; it constructs and returns a fastapi.params.Depends instance (params.py:746).

queries.query: What does FastAPI.add_api_route actually call to register the route?
queries.ground_truth_location: applications.py:1165 FastAPI.add_api_route calls self.router.add_api_route(...) at applications.py:1195, which is APIRouter.add_api_route at routing.py:2889
queries.expected_answer_summary: FastAPI.add_api_route() (applications.py:1165) forwards all its arguments to self.router.add_api_route() (APIRouter.add_api_route, routing.py:2889), which actually constructs the APIRoute and appends it to the router.

queries.query: What calls get_dependant() to build a route's dependency graph?
queries.ground_truth_location: fastapi/dependencies/utils.py:271 (def get_dependant); called from APIRoute's __init__ (routing.py, class at 1126) while constructing the route's Dependant tree
queries.expected_answer_summary: get_dependant() (dependencies/utils.py:271) is called when an APIRoute is constructed (routing.py:1126), building the Dependant object that solve_dependencies() later walks at request time.

queries.query: How does FastAPI resolve a path operation function's dependencies (Depends(...) parameters) at request time?
queries.ground_truth_location: get_dependant() (dependencies/utils.py:271) builds the Dependant tree when the route is registered; at request time get_request_handler()'s inner app() (routing.py:375, inner function at 406) calls solve_dependencies() (dependencies/utils.py:586) to actually resolve and call each dependency.
queries.expected_answer_summary: Each route's Depends() parameters are analyzed once at registration time into a Dependant tree by get_dependant() (dependencies/utils.py:271); on every request, the handler built by get_request_handler() (routing.py:375) calls solve_dependencies() (dependencies/utils.py:586), which recursively resolves and invokes each dependency callable.
queries.notes: multi-hop: registration-time graph building vs. request-time resolution are two different functions in two different call sites.

queries.query: How does FastAPI generate its OpenAPI schema?
queries.ground_truth_location: fastapi/openapi/utils.py:585 (def get_openapi), which calls get_openapi_path (openapi/utils.py:311) per route to build each path's operation object.
queries.expected_answer_summary: get_openapi() (openapi/utils.py:585) walks the app's registered routes and, for each one, calls get_openapi_path() (openapi/utils.py:311) to build that path's operation entry, assembling the full OpenAPI document.

queries.query: What happens when a request body fails Pydantic validation?
queries.ground_truth_location: fastapi/exceptions.py:212 (class RequestValidationError); the default handler is fastapi/exception_handlers.py:20 (request_validation_exception_handler), which returns a 422 JSONResponse.
queries.expected_answer_summary: A validation failure is raised as RequestValidationError (exceptions.py:212); FastAPI's default handler, request_validation_exception_handler (exception_handlers.py:20), catches it and returns a 422 response with the Pydantic error details as JSON.

queries.query: What response does FastAPI send back when a path operation raises HTTPException?
queries.ground_truth_location: fastapi/exceptions.py:17 (class HTTPException(StarletteHTTPException)); default handler at fastapi/exception_handlers.py:11 (http_exception_handler)
queries.expected_answer_summary: http_exception_handler() (exception_handlers.py:11) is FastAPI's default handler for HTTPException (exceptions.py:17); it returns a response using the exception's status_code and detail as the JSON body.

queries.query: Where would I look to debug why a FastAPI endpoint's OpenAPI docs are showing the wrong response schema?
queries.ground_truth_location: fastapi/openapi/utils.py:311 (get_openapi_path) reads response_model/response_class metadata off each APIRoute (routing.py:1126) to build the schema.
queries.expected_answer_summary: The OpenAPI schema per path comes from get_openapi_path() (openapi/utils.py:311), which reads the response_model and related fields stored on each APIRoute (routing.py:1126) -- a wrong schema traces back to how those fields were set when the route was registered (APIRouter.add_api_route, routing.py:2889).

queries.query: If a dependency function isn't being re-run per request when it should be, where should I look?
queries.ground_truth_location: fastapi/dependencies/utils.py:586 (solve_dependencies) -- this is where per-request dependency caching (use_cache) is implemented via a dependency cache keyed by the callable.
queries.expected_answer_summary: solve_dependencies() (dependencies/utils.py:586) is where per-request dependency resolution and its use_cache-based caching behavior live; unexpected re-use vs. re-execution of a dependency traces back to this function's cache-key logic.

queries.query: How does a security scheme like OAuth2PasswordBearer connect to a path operation's dependencies?
queries.ground_truth_location: OAuth2PasswordBearer (security/oauth2.py:433) subclasses OAuth2 (security/oauth2.py:330), itself a SecurityBase; when used as a Depends() default, get_dependant() (dependencies/utils.py:271) recognizes SecurityBase-typed dependencies specially so the OpenAPI schema records them as a security requirement.
queries.expected_answer_summary: OAuth2PasswordBearer (security/oauth2.py:433) is a callable SecurityBase subclass; when passed to Depends(), get_dependant() (dependencies/utils.py:271) special-cases SecurityBase dependencies so they're both resolved like any other dependency AND recorded as a security scheme for the OpenAPI schema.
queries.notes: cross-file: connects the security/ subpackage to the general dependency-injection machinery.

queries.query: Where does FastAPI implement its own SQL query builder or ORM?
queries.expected_answer_summary: FastAPI has no built-in ORM or SQL query builder in this repository. It is a web framework only; database access is expected to come from a separate library (e.g. SQLAlchemy) used by the application, not from FastAPI itself.

queries.query: Where does FastAPI implement built-in rate limiting for endpoints?
queries.expected_answer_summary: FastAPI has no built-in rate-limiting feature in this repository. Rate limiting is left to external middleware/packages (e.g. slowapi), not implemented here.
